text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that can understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are very useful for tasks like writing, translating and answering questions. However, they also have limits. They sometimes produce incorrect information, and their knowledge depends on the data they were trained on, so they may not always be reliable.
